title: From Sequential R&D to Trusted Co-Innovation: The EPIC Model for Semiconductor Innovation
gist: At the October 12, 2026 unveiling of Applied Materials' EPIC Center in Sunnyvale, CEO Gary Dickerson argued AI demands a shift from sequential R&D handoffs to early, parallel co-innovation across materials, transistors, interconnects, memory and packaging. The article frames trust as an operating requirement and EPIC as a physical venue for that model; it offers no figures.

themes.theme: From sequential handoffs to early co-innovation

insights.claim: Applied Materials CEO Gary Dickerson argued at the EPIC Center unveiling that AI's growing demands require a different R&D approach that brings partners together earlier across the whole semiconductor technology stack.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Applied is positioning itself as the hub of industry R&D, potentially deepening customer lock-in.

insights.claim: Sequential handoffs between technology developers, integrators and manufacturers break down when system performance depends on materials, equipment, transistors, interconnects, packaging, memory and architecture advancing together, because late discovery of dependencies causes costly redesigns and longer timelines.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Integration complexity raises the value of suppliers that coordinate across the stack.

themes.theme: Trust and the EPIC Center model

insights.claim: In co-innovation, trust is an operating requirement rather than a cultural aspiration, because partners in a competitive industry must share sensitive constraints and expertise under safeguards that define what can be discussed and how information is protected.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: IP protection frameworks determine whether rival chipmakers will co-develop at a shared center.
insights.quote: Trust is therefore more than a cultural aspiration. It is an enabler of technical progress.

insights.claim: Applied Materials' EPIC Center, unveiled October 12, 2026 in Sunnyvale, brings Applied and industry partners together to work on next-generation materials, processes and equipment, and its value will be measured by faster learning and technologies reaching manufacturing sooner.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Watch for named partners and faster tool adoption as evidence EPIC delivers.
